fix(run): honor requiredScripts in recursive runs
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpm v12 read no `requiredScripts` setting. `pnpm -r run <script>` ran normally even when a selected project lacked a script that pnpm-workspace.yaml lists as required. pnpm v11 fails that run before any script starts, with `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT` and `Missing script "<script>" in packages: <names>` (`throwIfRequiredScriptIsMissing` in `pnpm11/exec/commands/src/runRecursive.ts`). This PR adds the same behavior to v12.

- Config: `requiredScripts` is read from pnpm-workspace.yaml into `Config::required_scripts`. The global config.yaml drops it, as v11 does, because it is not a config-file key there. v11 reads no environment variable for it.
- Check: it runs where v11 runs it. That is after `--resume-from` and the `--dry-run` exit, and before the hidden-script filter and the no-script check. The `pnpm -r <script>` shorthand falls back to `exec` first, as in v11. A project is named by its manifest name, or by its directory if it has no name.
- Docs: the `requiredScripts` entry in both `pnpm/docs` and `pnpm11/docs` now says the check covers the projects selected for the run, not every workspace project.

Part of https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/191

prs.title: fix(help): accept --all and -a
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm help --all` and `pnpm help -a` failed in pnpm v12 with "unrecognized subcommand", because `help` is clap's built-in help subcommand, which declares no options. pnpm v11 accepts the flag (`pnpm11/pnpm/src/cmd/help.ts`) and uses it to list the commands its default help hides.

v12's plain `pnpm help` already lists every command, including all the ones v11 hides by default (`cat-index`, `find-hash`, `store`, `cache`, and so on). So the fix drops `--all`/`-a` from the arguments of `help` before clap parses argv, along with the other spellings v11's nopt Boolean accepts (`--all=<value>`, `--no-all`). The value is ignored, since v12's help is always the full list. Only tokens after the `help` subcommand are dropped: `pnpm run help -a` still passes `-a` to a script named `help` (unit test in `pnpm/crates/cli/src/tests.rs`).

`pnpm help help` does not list `--all` on purpose. It is clap's built-in help subcommand, which declares no options, and in v12 the flag changes nothing, because every command is listed already. Replacing clap's help subcommand only to document a flag that has no effect is not worth it. `pnpm help -a <command>` prints that command's help, as in v11. Plain `pnpm help` and `pnpm help <command>` print exactly what they printed before.

`pnpm/docs/cli/help.md` already describes `--all`/`-a`, so the docs are unchanged.

Part of https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/191

prs.title: fix(store): remove the metadata cache on store prune
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

In v12, `pnpm store prune` pruned the dlx cache, the global virtual store, and the content-addressable store, but it left the registry metadata cache in place. v11 removes that cache (`pnpm11/store/controller/src/storeController/prune.ts`), and the `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` advice in `pnpm/docs/errors.md` relies on it.

With this PR, v12 removes `<cacheDir>/metadata*` and `<cacheDir>/vN/metadata*`. That covers every mirror root v12 writes (`v12/metadata`, `v12/metadata-full`, `v12/metadata-full-filtered`, `v12/metadata-private`), the `v11/` legacy roots, and older top-level `metadata*` dirs. It runs between the GVS and CAS passes, under the exclusive store prune lock, which every install holds shared for its whole run. It prints v11's "Removed all cached metadata files". The v12 CAS prune already cleared `<storeDir>/tmp` (`remove_tmp`, which keeps private installs that are still held).

- **Narrower deletion.** v11 deletes every `vN` directory under `cacheDir` whole. In v12 that would also remove `v11/cargo-index`, `v11/tarball-resolutions`, and `v11/runtime-shasums`, so only the `metadata*` children of `vN` are removed.

fix(pnpr): record a token's last use off the request path, at most once a minute
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Every token-authenticated request awaited an `UPDATE tokens SET last_used_at` before its handler ran. With the libsql backend that write goes to the primary even when an embedded replica answers the lookup locally, so a replica removed almost none of the latency for authenticated traffic (p50 104 ms on a valid token against 0 ms on an unknown one, from the measurements in the task).

This PR takes both of the task's suggestions together. A new `LastUsedWriter` in `pnpr-auth`:

- skips the write while the stored time, which the authenticating lookup already read, is under a minute old;
- claims the interval per token in memory, so a burst of concurrent requests from one token writes once even before the first write lands or the replica syncs it back (the claim map prunes expired entries, amortized);
- runs the write in a spawned task the request never waits for. At most four writes run at once, since they share the token store's connection pool with the lookups that authenticate requests; a token refused a slot gives up its claim so its next request tries again. A failed write is logged at debug and retried by the next request past the interval.

Both middleware sites (bearer tokens, and the parent of an OCI token) go through it. The bearer site hands over the raw token, which the writer hashes with the auth crate's own key derivation and only once a write is due, so the server never derives token keys itself and the common path hashes the token once. `GET /-/npm/v
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(pnpr): emit the access record outside the request span
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes [pnpm/tasks#195](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/195).

With the default pretty format, every `pnpr::access` line printed each field twice and `user` three times. The access event was emitted inside the per-request span, which records the same fields, and the compact formatter appends the current span's fields after the event's. The JSON format hid the same duplication under a `span` object.

The access event now fires outside the request span. It already carries every documented field itself, so nothing is lost in either format, and the JSON access record becomes one flat object. The span keeps `request_id`, `method`, `uri`, `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and `user` for the events emitted inside a request: the audit records inherit the first four, and the authentication layer records `user` before the handler runs. The span's `status`, `latency_ms`, and `bytes` slots were only filled after the handler returned, when no event inside the request could see them, so they are removed.

The subscriber construction moves from `main.rs` into `pnpr::logging::log_subscriber` so the new test can run a request through the real pretty and JSON configurations and assert on the formatted line. The audit-log test now also captures values recorded on the span after it opens, and checks that the span's `user` matches the audit actor.

fix(add): accept the lowercase save aliases
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm add` now accepts `-p`, `-d`, `-o`, and `-e` as aliases of `--save-prod`, `--save-dev`, `--save-optional`, and `--save-exact`, matching pnpm v11's `add` shorthands (`pnpm11/installing/commands/src/add.ts`). The v12 docs already list them.

Only `add` declares these in v11, so `install` and `update` are unchanged. `pnpm install -d <pkg>` now resolves to `add` and saves to devDependencies, as in v11.

The aliases give `-o` and `-d` conflicting arity across subcommands (`pack-app -o <dir>` and `patch -d <dir>` take a value). The pre-subcommand scan in `flag_relocation` reads a conflicting short as boolean, which would have made `pnpm -o dist pack-app` and `pnpm -d dir patch` look like scripts named `dist` and `dir`. When the token that reading finds is not a command that declares the options written before it, the scan now retries with each subcommand's own arities, so both spellings still relocate and parse, including `pnpm -d edit patch foo` where the value is itself a command name. A moved option's value also stops before the command token, so `pnpm -o pack-app target` no longer drops `pack-app` from argv.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpm v12 had `Config::skip_runtimes` but nothing set it from configuration, so `runtime: false` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` was dropped and only `--no-runtime` skipped the runtimes from `devEngines.runtime` / `engines.runtime`. pnpm v11 honors the setting (`skipRuntimes: opts.runtime === false` in `pnpm11/installing/commands/src/installSingleProject.ts` and `recursive/context.ts`).

This PR makes v12 read `runtime` from the same sources v11 does: `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `pnpm_config_runtime` / `PNPM_CONFIG_RUNTIME`, and `--config.runtime`. The global `config.yaml` is left out, because `runtime` is in v11's `excludedPnpmKeys`. Every installing command follows it: `install`, `add`, `update`, `remove`, `deploy`, and now `dedupe` and `prune`, which used to force runtimes on. `pnpm dedupe` also accepts `--no-runtime`, as in v11. `updateConfig` hooks see `runtime` the way v11 shows it, and cannot undo `--no-runtime`.

prs.title: fix(store-dir): hold cache directories open while pruning their metadata
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#17253, which left [this review thread](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17253#discussion_r4354905452) open at merge time. The finding holds: `remove_cached_metadata` checked that a `vN` cache layout directory was a real directory, then re-resolved `<cacheDir>/vN/metadata*` by path for the removal. A process that can write to `cacheDir` could replace `vN` with a symbolic link between those steps and point the recursive removal at any `metadata*` directory the pruning user can delete.

The fix adds `pnpm_fs::OpenDir`, a directory held open while its children are opened or removed, and makes the prune use it for `cacheDir` and for each `vN`:

- On Unix, a child is opened through the parent's descriptor (`openat` with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY`) and removed through it as well: the removal walks the directory with `fdopendir` and `readdir` and unlinks every entry with `unlinkat`, relative to its parent descriptor. No step after the open resolves a path, so a link put in the place of `cacheDir` or of a `vN` directory cannot redirect it.
- The protection check for the store and the other protected directories compares against the opened directory's canonical path, which is verified to still name the opened directory (device and inode) before anything is removed. A replaced directory is skipped with a `tracing` warning.
- On Windows and WASI, `OpenDir` resolves the path for every operation, as the other symlink-safe helpers in the repo do there.

prs.title: fix(pnpr): time out libsql auth database dials and retry them at startup
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpr set no connect timeout on the libsql auth database connector, and it did not retry the startup connection. On a Cloudflare trial deployment, one dropped SYN at startup made pnpr wait out the kernel's TCP retransmissions, about two minutes, and then exit with `Auth database error: sync error: error trying to connect: tcp connect error: Connection timed out (os error 110)`.

- Every dial the libsql connector makes now times out after 10 seconds.
- While `LibsqlAuth::connect` runs (the protocol probe, the replica bootstrap, schema setup), a dial that timed out is retried with capped exponential backoff (250 ms doubling to 5 s). The whole startup now runs under one 5-minute deadline, which bounds the retries. Before, each step had a 5-minute deadline of its own. A refused connection or any other failure still fails at once, so a wrong URL or a rejected token is reported right away.
- After startup, a timed-out dial fails without a retry. Request-path writes run without a deadline, so they should not wait on retries.

Closes https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/199

## Squash Commit Body

```text

the kernel's retransmissions (about two minutes) before pnpr exited with
"tcp connect error: Connection timed out". On a platform that starts
instances on demand, that turned one lost packet into an outage.

- Every dial now times out after 10 seconds.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:

pnpm v12 read `strict-ssl` and `local-address` only from `.npmrc` and silently ignored `strictSsl` / `localAddress` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global `config.yaml`, and `PNPM_CONFIG_STRICT_SSL` / `PNPM_CONFIG_LOCAL_ADDRESS`. pnpm v11 reads them from all of these (they moved to the yaml files in b65204762a). Widening where a private key is read is left out on purpose.

Not covered: the bare `--strict-ssl` / `--local-address` flags (v11 accepts any nopt-typed setting as a bare flag; v12's `BARE_SETTING_FLAGS` does not list these). `--config.strict-ssl=...` works.

prs.title: fix(pnpr): delete the tarballs of versions a packument rewrite removes
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

A partial unpublish through a tar registry removed the version from the packument but left its `.tgz` downloadable. pnpr relied on the client to send the tarball DELETE. Clients take the filename from `dist.tarball`, which a tar registry leaves out. The packument rewrite now deletes the tarballs of the versions it removes.

Closes pnpm/tasks#202

## Squash Commit Body

```text
A partial unpublish rewrites the packument with `PUT /{package}/-rev/{rev}`
and then sends `DELETE /{package}/-/{filename}/-rev/{rev}` for the tarball,
taking the filename from `dist.tarball`. A tar registry leaves
`dist.tarball` out, so pnpm sent no DELETE and npm failed parsing the
missing URL. The version left the packument while its `.tgz` stayed
downloadable, because the tarball route reads the blob without the
packument.

The rewrite now deletes the `.tgz` and `.sigstore` blobs of every version
it removes, after the packument and tombstone writes. A client's later
tarball DELETE finds nothing and still succeeds.

Closes pnpm/tasks#202
```

prs.title: fix(local-resolver): resolve catalog dependencies of a package injected by a relative workspace path
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

A workspace package injected through a relative path (`workspace:../lib`) now resolves its `catalog:` dependencies through the catalogs, as one injected by name already does. Closes pnpm/pnpm#17280.

The deps resolver gates child catalog resolution on `resolvedVia === 'workspace'` plus a `file:` id. A relative `workspace:` specifier is declined by the npm resolver's workspace matching and claimed by the local resolver, which tagged every result `local-filesystem`, so the gate never saw it. The local resolver now tags a `workspace:` specifier `workspace`, the tag the name and range form gets, and the deps resolver is untouched.

This is an alternative to pnpm/pnpm#17295, which fixes the same issue by threading the wanted specifier into the gate in both deps resolvers (five source files and new parameters on `NodeIdentity`, `warm_grandchildren`, and `ParentPkg`). Fixing the tag where it is minted keeps the change to the two local resolvers, and every other reader of the tag sees the same answer for both forms of a `workspace:` specifier: the `blockExoticSubdeps` parent exemption, and the install's lockfile freshness check, which already treated a relative `workspace:` dependency as resolving through the catalogs.

fix(pnpr): verify OIDC workloads from issuers without an authorization endpoint
prs.author: spencerbeggs
prs.body:

GitHub Actions workload credentials (`pnpr_workload_<jwt>`) always fail with `500 OIDC provider unavailable`. pnpr ran discovery through `CoreProviderMetadata::discover_async`, and `openidconnect` 4.0.1 requires `authorization_endpoint`. GitHub Actions' discovery document has no `authorization_endpoint`, so parsing failed before any key was fetched.

Workload and ID-token verification use the key set. The login client uses the full metadata. All requests still go through the same transport, which allows only HTTPS and public addresses and caps responses at 1 MiB.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17300

prs.title: fix(resolver): resolve a workspace: path of an injected package from its directory
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17284.

When a workspace package is injected, its own dependencies are resolved by the walk as children of a `file:` package. A child `file:` path is already resolved from the declaring package's directory, but a `workspace:../lib-a` path kept the importer's directory (pnpm v12) or the lockfile directory (pnpm v11). So in the issue's layout the install looked for `apps/lib-a` and failed.

In pnpm v11 the redirect only applies when the `workspace:` path is itself injected. A linked one keeps its lockfile-relative id, because the linked node is registered under that id and the walk crashed otherwise (covered by the second v11 test). Not covered here: when the injected package's `workspace:` path stays linked (`dependenciesMeta` injection with `injectWorkspacePackages` off), both versions still write a link measured from the wrong directory, same as `link:../lib-a` does today.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17235.

With `autoDedupe` off (the default), every workspace project's manifest specifiers seeded the version picker for the whole workspace. A project's `ajv: "*"` therefore resolved to Ajv 6 because another project declared `^6.0.0`, while `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` gave it Ajv 8. That seeding is a partial dedupe. `pnpm dedupe` and `autoDedupe: true` merge more, and Yarn 4 and Bun resolve such a project independently ([comparison](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17235#issuecomment-6349772803)).

Now, unless `autoDedupe` is on or the command is `pnpm dedupe`:

- A project's dependencies resolve from its own ranges. The issue's consumer gets the latest Ajv.
- A project's own manifest specifiers (`Version`, `Range`, and `Tag`) still steer its own picks, so aliases, ranges, and pins inside one project resolve as before (pnpm/pnpm#15588). They form a root preference layer whose weight adds to the other layers, the way the seed's manifest entries did.

prs.author: zkochan

## Summary

pnpr served `/-/metrics` and `/metrics` to anyone. A deployment that did not filter them at a proxy published its request mix, cache hit rates, login throttling, and exact build version. pnpm/pnpm#17294 hid them in the Cloudflare Worker, but that only covers the Cloudflare recipe. This PR moves the decision into pnpr, using the usual industry patterns: off by default, a bearer token for scraping over the main port, and a dedicated listener for a private network.

```yaml
metrics:
  token: ${PNPR_METRICS_TOKEN}   # Prometheus `authorization.credentials`
  listen: 127.0.0.1:9464          # metrics only on this address
```

| Config | Main listener | Dedicated listener |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no `metrics` block | no metrics routes | none |
| `token` only | `/-/metrics` and `/metrics`, bearer required, else `401` | none |

| `token` and `listen` | no metrics routes | `GET /metrics`, bearer required |

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds the `symlinkedLockfileTargetDirs` setting (pnpm v12 only), a list of directories that defaults to empty. A lockfile write that changes `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves the symlink chain and, if the final target is inside one of the listed directories, atomically replaces it. Every link stays in place and the target keeps its file mode. Any other target, and every link when the list is empty, is refused as before. The refusal messages name the setting.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17222

Design notes:

- **A dedicated setting, not `trustLockfile`.** `trustLockfile` means "skip supply-chain verification of lockfile entries". Overloading it with "write through symlinks" would couple two unrelated decisions, so this follows the issue's second option.
- **No writer can skip the setting.** `Lockfile::save_to_path`, `save_value_to_path`, and `EnvLockfile::write` now take a `SymlinkedLockfile` (`Refuse` / `WriteThrough { allowed_dirs }`). Install, `--lockfile-only`, frozen relink, optimistic repeat install, pnpr-resolved installs, `patch-commit`, `import`, and the env-lockfile (config deps / packageManager pin) writers pass `config.symlinked_lockfile()`.
